3.title: Owners of agricultural land
paragraphs: Art. 3. (1) Agricultural land may be owned by citizens, the state, municipalities and legal entities.
(2) Political parties, organisations, movements and coalitions with political aims may not own agricultural land.
(3) Foreign states may not own agricultural land.

(4) Foreigners or foreign legal entities may acquire agricultural land under an international treaty ratified under Art. 22(2) of the Constitution, promulgated and in force, and foreigners also by legal inheritance.
(5) Citizens of EU Member States and EEA States may acquire agricultural land under this Act after the term set in the Treaty of Accession of Bulgaria to the EU.
(6) Legal entities from EU or EEA States may acquire agricultural land under para. 5.
(7) The following may not acquire or own agricultural land:
1. companies whose partners or shareholders are, directly or indirectly, companies registered in jurisdictions with a preferential tax regime;

2. companies whose partners or shareholders are foreigners other than the natural persons under paras. 4 and 5, or foreign legal entities other than those under paras. 4 and 6, and single-member companies founded by such persons;
3. joint-stock companies that issued bearer shares.
(8) Foreign legal entities and foreign citizens may acquire a right of use or other limited real rights in agricultural land under conditions and a procedure set by law.

3в.title: Residence requirement
paragraphs: Art. 3c. (1) Ownership of agricultural land may be acquired by natural or legal persons who resided or were established in Bulgaria for more than 5 years.
(2) Legal entities registered under Bulgarian law for less than 5 years may acquire agricultural land when their partners, members or founders meet the requirement of para. 1.
(3) When concluding the transaction, buyers who are natural persons present to the notary a declaration on the origin of the funds, and legal entities a document proving the origin of the funds.
(4) Para. 1 does not apply to acquisition of agricultural land by legal inheritance.

Art. 5. (1) The owners of agricultural land restored under this act are exempt from state fees, state notarial fees and local taxes and fees when they conclude agricultural lease contracts, lease contracts for more than 1 year, voluntary partitions and transactions of disposal of agricultural land, for 5 years.
(2) No state fee is due for the entry of decisions of the municipal agricultural office that have the force of a declaratory notarial deed of ownership.

(3) For the certification of the signatures of the parties to written agricultural lease contracts and lease contracts for agricultural land, a notarial fee is charged regardless of the material interest or the time spent, in the amount set by the tariff under Art. 85(3) of the Notaries and Notarial Activity Act. When the signatures of the parties are certified at the same time, the fee is charged once.

Art. 10. (1) The rights of the owners or their heirs are restored to the agricultural land that they owned before the labour cooperative farms or the state farms were formed, whether or not the land was included in them or in other agricultural organisations formed on their basis.
(2) The rights of the owners are restored to the agricultural land nationalised under the repealed Art. 12 of the Citizens' Property Act, after the money compensation received is returned.
(3) The rights of the owners who gave their land free of charge to a labour cooperative farm or to the state are restored.
(4) The rights of the owners are restored to agricultural land taken from them unlawfully.

(5) The rights of the owners are restored to forested and self-forested agricultural land, including agricultural land for which the owners were not compensated and which was included in the State Forest Fund, except forest nurseries and protective forest belts. The ownership is restored under Art. 14(1), item 1.

(6) The rights of the owners are restored to yards managed as agricultural land by a labour cooperative farm, a state farm or other agricultural organisations formed on their basis, in settlements that were struck off or abandoned.

(7) The rights of the owners are restored to agricultural land owned before the labour cooperative farms and state farms were formed, whether or not it was included in them or in other agricultural organisations formed on their basis, and included in the boundaries of the urbanised territories (settlements) set by a detailed development plan or a ring polygon, unless buildings were built on it by third persons in compliance with all regulations, or a building right was given and the lawfully permitted construction had started by 1 March 1991. The ownership is restored under Art. 14(1), item 1.

(8) The rights of the owners of agricultural land are restored up to the sizes set by the repealed Art. 8(1) and Art. 10 of the Labour Land Ownership Act, including land expropriated under that act. For agricultural land above these sizes, the owners are compensated under Art. 35. The limit on the size also applies when the agricultural land was confiscated by a sentence and the sentence was set aside.
(9) At the request of the owners, ownership is restored of land nationalised as forests and later turned into agricultural land.

(10) Polluted, eroded, salinised, acidified and surface-waterlogged agricultural land is returned to the owners, and the state bears the costs of its recovery. The funds for restoring the productive qualities of this land, including for blocking dangerous pollutants, come from the budget of the Ministry of Agriculture and Food under a programme approved each year by the Council of Ministers. The Council of Ministers sets the procedure and the ways of cleaning the land and of controlling polluted agricultural land.
(11) Ownership is restored to the persons given land under the Labour Land Ownership Act, including those who did not fully pay the instalments due, except those from whom the land was taken back.

(12) The rights of the owners are restored under Art. 14(1), item 1 to the land inside and outside the boundaries of the urbanised territories (settlements) included in the farmyards of labour cooperative farms, state farms or other agricultural organisations formed on their basis, which is not built on and is not land adjoining buildings.

(13) Ownership is restored of the land owned before the labour cooperative farms, state farms or other agricultural organisations formed on their basis were formed, which these organisations or other state or municipal bodies sold or gave to third persons, except in the cases expressly set in this act. The acquirers cannot rely on acquisitive prescription.

(14) Land taken from its owners under the Ordinance-Act on the trial by the People's Court, the Act on the Confiscation of Property Acquired by Speculation or Unlawfully, the Act on the Collection of Taxes and Other State Receivables, the Ordinance on the Collection of Taxes and Fees, the Ordinance-Act on Supply and Prices, the Decree on the compulsory re-registration of uncovered agricultural properties, and under the decrees of the Council of Ministers of 1951, 1952 and 1958 listed in this paragraph, is also subject to restitution. [The State Gazette references are omitted.]
Art. 14. (1) The municipal agricultural office decides on:

1. the restitution of the right of ownership of land in existing or restorable old real boundaries on the ground. The decision describes the size and the category of the property, its location (boundaries, neighbours) and the restrictions on the ownership with their grounds. A sketch of the property is attached to the decision. The final decision with the sketch, except in the cases under Art. 10(7), certifies the right of ownership and has the force of a declaratory notarial deed of ownership of the property. When the decision restores the ownership of agricultural land of a deceased owner, it is issued jointly for the heirs. The shares of the heirs are set under the Inheritance Act and are not stated in the decision;

2. the restitution of the right of ownership of agricultural land in new real boundaries with a plan for land division. The decision states the size and the categories of the land and the area of the village land where it was. The plan for land division is made on the basis of the decisions of the municipal agricultural office after study, survey and design, and after a survey of at least half of the owners or their heirs, in the procedure of the implementing regulations. The need to revise the plan is set by an order of the Minister of Agriculture and Food or an official designated by the minister;
3. the recognition of the right of ownership under the conditions of § 4–4l; the decision describes the size and the area where the agricultural land was.
(2) The decision of the municipal agricultural office is communicated to the persons concerned under the Civil Procedure Code.

(3) The decisions of the municipal agricultural office may be appealed within 14 days before the district court. The appeal is filed through the office. The court decides the dispute on the merits. The cases are heard in the settlement where the property is. The decision of the district court may be appealed in cassation before the administrative court under the Administrative Procedure Code, which hears it in a panel of three judges.
(4) In a dispute about a substantive right, the persons concerned exercise their rights in court.
(5) All evidence under the Civil Procedure Code is admissible in the proceedings before the district court.
(6) The municipal agricultural office may correct obvious factual errors in its decision of its own motion or at the request of the persons concerned.

(7) When breaches of this act or its implementing regulations, new circumstances or new written evidence of substantial importance for the decision under para. 1 are discovered, within one year of the discovery, but not later than three years from the entry into force of the plan for land division or from the decision under para. 1, item 1, the Minister of Agriculture and Food, of the minister's own motion or at the request of the persons concerned, cancels the decision or orders the office to change it. This procedure does not apply when there is a final court decision for the same land.
(7a) The persons concerned may ask the municipal agricultural office, under the conditions and procedure of para. 7, to change the persons in whose favour or against whom the decision was issued.
(7b) The terms under para. 7 do not run when the decision was issued in breach of Art. 16(3) of the Waters Act.

(8) The decisions under paras. 6 and 7 are communicated under para. 2 and may be appealed under the procedure and within the terms of para. 3. When the decisions are made after the State Gazette announced that a draft plan for land division was prepared, the owners are compensated under Art. 10b.
(9) The municipal agricultural office is represented before the court by its head, deputy head, an authorised person with a law degree, or the Ministry of Agriculture and Food.
